title: Review of c48's CIPS turnover window on fresh seed 5: doubled turnover gives one small non-dividing g2 dot and halved turnover a giant g2 filament with slower g1 division, as claimed; but the filament pinches off its end at t~8400
summary: Labkit re-runs of the finding's world.py (192^2, 100 frames to t=10000) on fresh seed 5 with WORLD_P {b2: 1.0 or -0.5, inoc_mix: 1}; per-kind counts from the frames (scripts/kinds.py; e>0.5, >=10 px, kind by larger mean label). The coin gave one g2 body among 6. b2=+1: the g2 body stays single and shrinks from 110 to 94 px; g1 bodies go 5 -> 12. b2=-0.5: the g2 body grows into a filament across the periodic box (443 -> 1062 px by t=7500) while g1 bodies go only 5 -> 9; at t~8400 the filament's end bulb pinches off and both g2 pieces persist to t=10000 (905-990 and ~280 px; g2_filament_s5.png).

observations.D: kinds_b1.0.json: g2 1 -> 1 (no division, area 110 -> 94 px), g1 5 -> 12; kinds_b-0.5.json: g2 filament 1062 px at t=7500, g1 5 -> 9 (fewer g1 divisions than the b2=+1 box, the neighbour stall); g2_filament_s5.png: one pinch-off of the filament end at t~8400

seeds_run.result: pass for b2=+1; b2=-0.5 gives the filament and the g1 stall, with one late pinch-off of the filament end

controls_run.D: the g1 bodies in the same boxes (default turnover) serve as the in-box control, as in the finding

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed, one g2 body per box. The finding's 'never pinch' for halved turnover holds only to t~8000 here: a 1000 px filament sheds its end bulb at t~8400, so halved turnover delays division a lot rather than stopping it. The window statement (division only near the ancestral turnover) otherwise stands.
